title: Pulsebridge 48h deploy calendar and release digest
content:
Overview:

This doc is an operational scribble for the Pulsebridge incremental surge: a controlled, 48-hour deploy window focused on low-latency model routing changes and a small batch of performance optimizations. Purpose is to provide: a compact hour-by-hour calendar, steward handoffs, quick runbook checklists for on-call and release stewards, and a first-pass release-notes draft to share with product and CSM before the public digest.

Tone: pragmatic, checklist-forward, lightweight. This is intentionally informal — fill in missing links and callouts as you Triaged them.

High level goals:
- Gradual routing change: move 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 48h with safety holds.
- Validate latency SLOs for p95/p99 and ensure cost delta < 12% vs baseline.
- Confirm fallback variants and the cold-path revert are working end-to-end.

Key owners (day-of):
- Release steward: Aisha Patel (primary contact)
- Traffic shepherd: Liam Rodriguez (adjusts routing weights)
- Runtime lead: Emily Chen (hotfixes, kernel rollbacks)
- SRE/observability: Marcus Ivanov (dashboards, sampling, alert tuning)
- Customer comms: Priya Malhotra (CSM)

Signals and thresholds (hard gates):
- Telemetry: p95 latency increase > 18% sustained for 10m -> HOLD and evaluate.
- Errors: 5xx rate > 0.3% relative increase vs baseline for 5m -> HOLD.
- Cost: unit token cost increase > 20% -> notify finance and consider throttle.
- Quality: automated eval set (smoke prompts) F1 drop > 6% -> auto-revert scenario.

Pulsebridge 48h calendar (compact)

Day -2 (prep)
- [ ] Finalize routing config and export JSON to release repo. (GH PR linked above)
- [ ] Run a quick canary in sandbox for 1 hour at 10rps; collect KV cache warmup metrics.
- [ ] Update telemetry sampling to 100% for p95/p99 trace tags for next 24h.
- [ ] Draft customer-facing line items for release notes (see below).

Day -1 (dry run + comms)
- Morning: preflight sync 30m with owners; confirm runbook roles and pager responder list.
- Afternoon: dry-run cut to preprod with rolled weights: 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> revert. Capture differences.
- Evening: send pre-announce to beta customers and internal Slack channel #launch-pulsebridge.

Deploy window (Day 0) — Hour by hour (start 09:00 PT)
- 09:00 — Preflight checklist (15m):
  - [ ] Pager contacts on-call and stewards acknowledged.
  - [ ] Smoke test harness (10 prompts) passing locally.
  - [ ] Canary route manifests uploaded (S3 path: s3://releases/pulsebridge/2026-05-14).
- 09:15 — Start: 5% traffic for 30m
  - [ ] Observe latency signals; snapshot dashboards.
  - [ ] Run automated evals (quality smoke) and post to the digest channel.
- 09:45 — If green, increase to 25% for 1h
- 10:45 — Evaluate; if green, increase to 60% for 3h
- 13:45 — Midday check-in with exec-synthesis (10m)
  - [ ] Confirm cost delta and p95/p99; check sampling heatmap.
- 14:00 — If stable, go to 100% for 24h with staggered rollback windows (15m checkpoints).

Contingency lanes (quick reference)
- Soft revert (minutes): shift routing to previous variant via routing key rollback. Documented command: /opt/bin/route-shift --from pulsebridge-v2 --to pulsebridge-v1 --weight 100
- Emergency cut: drain all requests to fallback pool (fallback name: pb-fallback-quantized). Notify customer comms.
- Patch flow: small binary hotfix -> stage -> 5% -> 100% (repeat 48h cadence).

Operator checklists (concise)
- Release steward (Aisha):
  - [ ] Confirm PR merge and artifact integrity.
  - [ ] Execute routing weight changes in the orchestration UI and document times.
  - [ ] Run release notes publish to internal channel after 100% stable for 1h.
- Traffic shepherd (Liam):
  - [ ] Monitor route weight transitions; hold if threshold breached.
  - [ ] Coordinate any rollbacks with steward and SRE.
- Runtime lead (Emily):
  - [ ] Watch kernel-level errors, GPU OOM, and model serving restarts.
  - [ ] Prepare quick-rollback artifact and container image tag to revert.
- Observability (Marcus):
  - [ ] Ensure trace samples are being collected and logged.
  - [ ] Tweak alert thresholds temporarily if we see noisy signals (document changes).

Post-deploy (Day 1 to Day 2)
- First 1h of 100%: intensive sampling and customer ping list; record anomalies.
- 6h after 100%: run an extended quality eval across 50 curated prompts (open issues if F1 drop > 3%).
- 24h after 100%: compile the release digest and preliminary retrospective notes.
- 48h: finalize release notes for external publish and archive the increment manifest.

Release notes (draft — internal first pass)
- Short blurb for product release email: "Pulsebridge routing improvements: reduced tail latency for low-context chat flows, and smarter cache warmup across shards. Rolling release over 48h starting 2026-05-14; see internal digest for details."

- What changed (technical):
  - Adjusted routing policy to prefer locality-aware subpools for short-sequence requests.
  - Introduced prefix-KV prewarming for the top 10 frequent prefixes to reduce kv-cache misses.
  - Tuned batching heuristics to be more aggressive at 1–3k concurrent connections.

- Why this matters (customer-friendly):
  - 10–18% p95 latency improvement observed in internal benchmarks for short-turn chat.
  - More consistent performance during surge windows and lower cost for many common usage patterns.

- Known limitations and notes:
  - Small subset of long-context workflows may see negligible change; we are continuing evals.
  - If you rely on exact-cost accounting at token level, expect short-term sampling variation during the 48h ramp.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Verify the sampling retention TTL for traces; current retention may drop important cold-start traces after 6h.
- Should we add a one-click rollback button in the orchestration UI for future pulse releases? (ask UX/product)
- Cross-check with finance: confirm whether cost-budget guardrails should trip an automated slow-down.

Appendix: quick commands and breadcrumbs
- Routing manifest location: s3://releases/pulsebridge/2026-05-14/manifest.json
- Revert command (example): /opt/bin/route-shift --to pb-previous --weight 100 --note "emergency revert 2026-05-14"
- Debug snapshot: /tmp/pulsebridge-dbg-<timestamp>.tgz (collect on runtime host)

End of doc — leave comments below and I will fold into a final release digest tomorrow morning once we have 24h of post-rollout telemetry.

-- Aisha
